long_biography.plain_text:
Direct factory sourcing gave Eric Smidt the model that turned Harbor Freight from a mail-order catalogue into a national tool retailer. As a teenager, he joined his father Allan's small telephone-sales business and helped recast it around tools bought without intermediaries. Smidt later became president, bought his father's stake and remains owner and chief executive.

Harbor Freight paired its store expansion with in-house engineering and testing of tools sold under exclusive brands, retaining the low-price logic of the catalogue business. Smidt also created Harbor Freight Tools for Schools through his foundation. The programme supports welding, construction, automotive and other skilled-trades teaching in American public high schools.
